correctness.rationale: Starting from the source's closed reduced-density-matrix formula, the package expression agrees with an independent density-matrix/Wootters calculation in the inspected verifier. For the activation threshold, writing \(q=e^{3J/T}\) makes the arcosh argument one plus \(12/q+O(q^{-2})\), giving \(\sqrt6\,Tq^{-1/2}\). In the critical scaling \(B=3J/2+sT\), the partition function and concurrence numerator share the factor \(e^{(9J/2T)+s}\), leaving the finite ratio \(2/[3(2+e^{2s})]\), which reproduces one-third, two-ninths and zero in the three limiting directions. For fixed supercritical field the next Boltzmann sector yields the stated Arrhenius exponent and coefficient.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a genuine noncommuting-limit phenomenon at the quantum saturation transition: a pointwise zero-temperature jump becomes a universal width-O(T) crossover, while field activation near zero field occurs on an exponentially smaller scale. final_claim: For the antiferromagnetic three-qubit XXX ring, the field-induced entanglement has two distinct low-temperature scales: the activation threshold obeys \(B_*(T)\sim\sqrt6\,T e^{-3J/(2T)}\), while at the saturation field \(B_c=3J/2\) the crossover \(B=B_c+sT\) has limiting concurrence \(2/[3(2+e^{2s})]\); for fixed \(B>B_c\), concurrence has the Arrhenius tail \((2/3)e^{-2(B-B_c)/T}\).
limitations: Specific to pairwise concurrence in the three-site periodic antiferromagnetic XXX model.
